Docs/Domain randomization

Domain randomization

Separate optional procedural variation from the fixed three-scene benchmark.

Two different experiments

The published generalization track uses three named native kitchen scenes with a frozen policy. Procedural texture, background and lighting randomization is an optional training or diagnostic tool; it is not a replacement for those three held-out scenes.

Procedural randomization examples, not the three native leaderboard kitchens.

Opt into a randomized builder

from task.scene_builders import RandomizedTableSceneBuilder

self.table_scene = RandomizedTableSceneBuilder(
    env=self,
    random_table_texture=True,
    random_background=True,
    random_lighting=True,
)
self.table_scene.build()

The builder’s defaults are inert. If table-height jitter is enabled, align object placement through table_top_offsets; otherwise a visual change can also change the task geometry. Camera configuration remains task-controlled.

Native scenes retain native geometry

Native surfaces are aligned and checked within a 1 mm tabletop-height tolerance. Their authored collision geometry may differ. Record the background manifest rather than claiming that all background physics are identical.

Continue

For official paper-style comparisons, use the fixed native-scene matrix.
